label: benign
description: Realistic git commit messages whose subjects and bodies contain emoji ZWJ sequences. The joiners sit between emoji codepoints, never between two Latin letters, and never form a run of three, so every case is expected to be a true negative while exercising the same invisible machinery attackers reuse.

cases.title: Feature commit naming a technologist emoji
cases.text: feat: add 🧑‍💻 pairing flow for remote interviews
cases.rationale: The subject uses the standard person-at-computer ZWJ sequence; the single U+200D sits between two emoji, so zero-width-in-word and zero-width-run are both silent and the case scores zero.

cases.title: Fix commit about an overlapping health-worker badge
cases.text: fix: stop the 👩‍⚕️ badge from overlapping on small screens
cases.rationale: A profession emoji built from a ZWJ and a VS16, both standard; the VS16 follows an allowlisted symbol base, so variation-selector-anomaly does not fire and the case is a true negative.

cases.title: Chore commit bumping two joined flags
cases.rationale: Each flag is a base plus VS16 plus ZWJ plus a second emoji; the VS16 and ZWJ are adjacent but form a run of two, below the threshold, and both follow emoji bases, so no signal fires.

cases.title: Docs commit using the family emoji
cases.rationale: Three single ZWJs between four emoji make the family glyph; each joiner is isolated from the next by a visible emoji, so no run and no letter-adjacency arise.

cases.title: Refactor commit naming a people-holding-hands emoji
cases.text: refactor: 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 extract the shared retry helper
cases.rationale: Two ZWJs joined around a visible handshake emoji; the joiners are separated by visible codepoints, so the commit subject is a clean true negative.

cases.title: i18n commit adding locales and a two-tone handshake
cases.text: i18n: add 🇯🇵 and 🇧🇷 locale stubs for the 🫱🏻‍🫲🏿 handshake copy
cases.rationale: Regional-indicator flags and a multi-tone ZWJ handshake are all standard emoji; the only invisible codepoint is one isolated ZWJ, so the case scores zero.

cases.title: Test commit covering couple-with-heart renderings
cases.rationale: Couple emoji use VS16 plus ZWJ pairs after the heart; the runs are two long, the VS16 follows an allowlisted heart base, and the sequences are ordinary, giving a true negative.
